findings.finding: The replacement iterate-count command `grep -c '"type": "work_completed"' shipwright_events.jsonl` undercounts ~5x. The events writer switched to compact JSON separators partway through the file: this repo has 103 lines with `"type": "work_completed"` and 419 with `"type":"work_completed"` (522 total, all source=iterate). The prescribed command returns 103 and the gap widens with every new event, since all new rows use the compact form.
findings.suggestion: Use `grep -c '"type": *"work_completed"' shipwright_events.jsonl` (matches both spacings) or `grep -c '"work_completed"'`; add a PowerShell equivalent alongside it, matching the new wc -c/wc -l PS block.

findings.finding: "this repo's own actual average is higher (several entries per iterate on a busy one), so in practice this repo crossed each line sooner" is derived from the undercounted iterate figure. Measured: 347 `### ADR-` entries in decision_log.md against 522 work_completed events = 0.66 entries per iterate, i.e. below one-per-iterate, so this repo crossed each threshold LATER than the iterate-count column suggests, not sooner.
findings.suggestion: Reword to the measured direction (fewer than one decision entry per iterate on average, so the iterate-count column runs ahead of reality here) once the grep in line 29 is corrected; keep the 'trust the byte/line count' conclusion, which holds either way.

findings.finding: The readiness command example presents optional arguments in square brackets inside a shell code block. Copying it verbatim passes literal `[`/`]` arguments to `context_cost_readiness.py`, which will fail argument parsing rather than perform the readiness check.
findings.suggestion: Show a valid command without optional arguments, then provide a separate valid example with concrete values (for example, `--model <model-id> --effort <level>`), or place the bracket notation outside the executable code block.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The threshold-based document, guide additions, README link, transferability caveats, and opt-in framing satisfy the requested deliverables; the executable command example should be corrected before shipping. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
